title.purpose: Bold app title, with tail truncation.

body.purpose: Buttons, duration picker, and explanatory copy.

label.purpose: Status, wrapped hints, opacity, preview percentages, and text-size captions.

motion.name: transition-easing
motion.purpose: Smoothstep interpolation of object position, size, opacity, and font size; t is clamped from 0 to 1.

motion.name: trigger-hold
motion.purpose: Show the initial pose and trigger before the transition.

motion.name: end-hold
motion.purpose: Hold the end pose after the transition.

motion.name: transition-duration
motion.purpose: Duration picker choices; the document default is 1000ms.

breakpoints.name: side-controls
breakpoints.purpose: At this root width, a 320dp scrolling control panel sits to the left of the canvas workspace with a 12dp gap. The workspace retains its 60dp text-size rail.

components.name: Primary action
components.description: Export and Play. Browser preview maps 1dp to 1 CSS px and baseline sp to px; browser hover and focus are illustrative.

components.name: Light tonal action
components.description: Secondary action in light theme. Disabled appearance and interaction feedback remain Android-owned in the app.

components.name: Dark tonal action
components.description: Secondary action in dark theme. Browser preview only.

components.name: Draw and Animate
components.description: Equal-width mode buttons. Selected mode has a native semantic description and Android Selected state. This static HTML preview shows Draw selected.
components.html: <nav class="ds-modes" aria-label="Sketch mode"><button class="ds-button ds-mode ds-selected" aria-pressed="true">Draw</button><button class="ds-button ds-mode" aria-pressed="false">Animate</button></nav>

components.name: Canvas viewport actions
components.description: Below the mode buttons, dimensions open a native sheet with named presets, Rotate swaps width and height, and Fit restores the whole-paper view. This browser preview shows the row without implementing its actions; 1 CSS px represents 1dp.

components.name: Drawing tools
components.description: Scrollable labeled tools preserve their width. This static browser preview shows Select selected; Android owns touch scrolling.

components.name: Sketch text entry
components.description: Tonal editor with a 160dp native minimum height, 20sp text, and a 300-character limit. This browser textarea does not reproduce native autosizing, keyboard handwriting, or speech recognition.
components.html: <textarea class="ds-editor" aria-label="Text for your sketch" maxlength="300" placeholder="Type, write with your S Pen, or use the microphone"></textarea>

components.name: Preview progress
components.description: Native Slider has a blue thumb and filled track, tonal remaining track, and a semantic description. Browser range geometry is illustrative and does not update the static caption.

components.name: Text-size rail
components.description: Persistent 60dp rail beside the canvas. The native rotated Slider enlarges selected text upward and commits one Undo step per drag. A disabled control shows Select text. This browser range illustrates placement and states; its caption is static and it does not reproduce Android range semantics or text fitting.

components.name: Pen only
components.description: Android Switch uses blue when on and has a semantic description explaining finger rejection for drawing. Two-finger navigation remains available. The browser checkbox represents the setting; it is not a native switch replica.

components.name: Paper and selected object
components.description: Illustrative SVG at one document unit per dp. Grid dots are spaced 16 document units apart. The native 4dp selection inset, 8dp handle radius, and 24dp resize hit tolerance remain stable on screen through fit and zoom; this static SVG does not simulate that compensation.

components.name: Trigger annotation
components.description: Renderer marker and rounded caption in document units. This static SVG shows a tap annotation; browser focus and motion are not native trigger behavior.

narrative.overview:
White paper holds the drawing. Blue marks the chosen tool, editing state, and animation trigger. The surrounding Android controls use slate tones and system text. The canvas takes the space left by the controls, with a persistent text-size rail at its right edge.

This records the built MAUI interface. The notebook description comes from the implementation; it is not a separately approved concept. Native measurements below use dp for layout and sp for interface text. Canvas measurements use document units, labeled px in the text-size control, and scale with the paper. Selection affordances retain their screen size. The sidecar's browser previews and synthesized color ramps are illustrative, not native specifications.
keyCharacteristics: Monochrome artwork on white dotted paper.
Native controls with readable labels and horizontally scrolling tool rows.
A shared, zoomable canvas for Draw and Animate, with named viewport presets.

rules.name: The Paper Rule
rules.body: Keep the document white and its artwork monochrome when the surrounding interface changes theme.

rules.name: The Native Text Rule
rules.body: Preserve system font scaling for interface text and keep canvas text sizing tied to the document.

dos: Do keep paper, ink, and grid colors stable across app themes.
Do preserve the minimum 48dp button targets and 8dp horizontal control gaps.
Do let tool rows scroll, hints wrap, and the title truncate as interface text grows.
Do keep the text-size rail visible and selection affordances stable while the paper zooms.
Do use the scrolling control panel at 640dp root width and above.
Do pair selected colors with the existing semantic selected state.
Do keep motion, opacity, and trigger feedback in the shared document view.
donts: Don't invert the artwork when applying dark theme to the controls.
Don't treat canvas document units as dp or sp.
Don't export selection handles or the editing grid.
Don't copy browser-preview focus styles or synthesized ramps into the native theme as established tokens.
